rationale: Evidence from R2A: all 60 trials (oval, s-bend, slalom) ended off_track with 0 finishes. Progress was only 0.04 to 0.12, and every trial logged one line_loss_event. Max error was about 0.061 m, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit, so the robot lost the line early and drifted off. Steering oscillation (0.06 to 0.07) and control effort are low, so the loop is not jittering. The failure is a loss of line tracking, not a speed or time problem, so completion_time and base_speed should not be the first changes. Changes: (1) kp 3.0 to 2.0. The baseline turn of up to about 1050 PWM likely overshot on entry to bends and pushed the robot off the tape; a gentler gain should keep the line in view. (2) kd 0.05 to 0.15 to damp the faster response that lower kp gives. (3) sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016 so each footprint covers more of the 25 mm tape and fewer readings drop below the 0.05 line-loss threshold. (4) base_speed 1.6 to 1.4 to reduce the lateral drift per step while the tracking is unproven; this trades some completion-time margin for a better chance of finishing. (5) line_loss kept at last_direction, since the evidence does not yet say which way the line is lost. Expected result: line_loss_events drops toward 0, max_error stays under 0.06, and progress rises well above 0.5 on the development tracks. Hypotheses to check: H1, the early off-track is caused by overshoot at bend entry (watch max_error vs. time). H2, line loss comes from sensors dropping below threshold between footprints (watch line_loss_events with sensor_size change). Next measurements wanted: per-track progress, max_error, line_loss_events, and steering_oscillation, so I can tell whether the gain or the sensor coverage was the driver.
